title: Unawareness of continuous sensor data capture
description: Wearer may not realize the extent of telemetry (heart rate, steps, GPS, timestamps) being continuously shared with the device simply by wearing it.
assumptions: User has not been explicitly informed of all data types captured in real-time.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate based on standard LINDDUN U category for unawareness of collection

title: Linkability of location and biometric traces over time
description: Continuous flow of GPS positions with timestamps and heart rate enables linking successive activities to the same individual.
assumptions: Data elements are transmitted together without sufficient anonymization or separation.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; this is a data-centric meta-data linking threat on the flow

title: Disclosure of sensitive health and location data on device
description: Wearable device (process) receives and may store/process raw sensor telemetry containing identifiable and sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Device has local storage or further processing that retains the data.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate for disclosure upon receipt

title: Identifiability via device ID and location data
description: Wearable device (P1) shares batches containing device ID, timestamps, and GPS traces, enabling the recipient to identify the individual user.
assumptions: Device ID is unique and GPS traces can be correlated to known locations or home/work.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate without full threat tree reference

title: Disclosure of sensitive sensor data in transit
description: Sensor batches with exercise sessions and GPS are transmitted over the flow, risking interception if not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Sync may occur over untrusted networks like public WiFi.

title: Linkability of sessions at the companion app
description: Companion app (P2) receives and processes multiple syncs, allowing linking of exercise sessions over time to build user profiles.
assumptions: App stores historical data without sufficient anonymization.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate without full threat tree reference

title: Unawareness of privacy implications when logging sensitive data
description: User manually entering calorie intake, meals, and weight may not realize the extent of data processing, storage, or potential sharing with third parties by the companion app.
assumptions: App processes this personal health data for features like tracking or recommendations.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate based on standard LINDDUN unawareness categories; exact tree may vary.

title: Disclosure of personal health information
description: The companion mobile app receives and handles sensitive data including meals, calories, and weight entries, risking unauthorized disclosure if access controls or encryption are insufficient.
assumptions: Data is stored or processed within the app after logging.

title: Linkability of health logs to user identity
description: The data flow of manual entries could enable linking of specific dietary and weight patterns to the identifiable user if metadata or logs are accessible.
assumptions: Flow involves some form of identifiable input or session.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if flow involves network transit or is purely local input; node id approximate.

title: Disclosure of sensitive health data at storage
description: Health logs containing calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions are stored in DS1, which if accessed improperly could disclose highly sensitive personal health information.
assumptions: The datastore is accessible to app backend or admins.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate as exact LINDDUN Pro tree not referenced; based on standard disclosure threats for stored PII/health data.

title: Interception during data transmission
description: Sensitive health logs written from P2 to DS1 over the data flow could be intercepted if encryption is insufficient.
assumptions: Mobile app communicates over potentially insecure networks.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; typical for data-in-transit disclosure in LINDDUN.

title: Unawareness of data logging and storage
description: Users of the Companion Mobile App may be unaware that their detailed health logs are being persistently stored in the Health Log Store.
assumptions: App UI may not clearly inform users about backend storage.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate based on standard unawareness threats for data sharing acts.

title: User unawareness of location tracking
description: The companion app writes detailed GPS traces without sufficiently informing the user about the storage and potential use of their location history.

title: Disclosure of precise location history
description: The location history datastore retains timestamped GPS traces that can reveal sensitive personal movements and routines to anyone with access to the store.

title: Linkability via metadata in transit
description: Writing location data creates a flow that can link successive GPS points to the same user identity through timing and data patterns.

title: Identifiability from stored traces
description: Stored location history with timestamps allows re-identification of the individual even if initially anonymized, due to unique movement patterns.

title: Disclosure of sensitive health data during transmission
description: The flow of calorie, weight, and exercise logs from the Health Log Store to the Analytics Service may disclose personal health information if the data in transit is not adequately protected (e.g., lack of encryption).
assumptions: Assumes the data flow occurs over a network or channel that could be intercepted.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate based on typical LINDDUN disclosure threats for data flows; no reference material available.

title: Linkability of health sessions by analytics process
description: The Health Analytics Service reading logs across sessions enables linking of user activities (calories, weight, exercise) over time, potentially creating detailed behavioral or health profiles.
assumptions: The analysis explicitly uses cross-session data as described.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as plausible for linkability via data aggregation; uncertain without exact LINDDUN Pro tree.

title: User unawareness of data usage for analytics
description: Users whose health logs are stored in DS1 may be unaware that their data is being read and analyzed by P3 for health-condition analysis.
assumptions: No explicit consent or notice mechanism mentioned in the flow description.

title: Linkability through cross-session location queries
description: Analytics service links location history across sessions to derive daily routines and movement patterns, enabling user profiling and identification of sensitive behaviors.
assumptions: Location data contains timestamps and coordinates sufficient for pattern recognition.

title: Disclosure of inferred personal routines
description: Deriving movement patterns from location history discloses sensitive information about user's daily life, habits, and potentially health-related movements.
assumptions: The service has access to raw location data without sufficient anonymization.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate based on typical disclosure threats in processing.

title: Unawareness of secondary use for analytics
description: Data store shares location history for analytics without ensuring user awareness or consent for deriving routines and patterns.
assumptions: Users consented to storage but not explicitly to this analysis flow.

title: Disclosure of health insights during transmission
description: Sensitive health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags returned from the analytics service could be intercepted or eavesdropped on the data flow to the companion app, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of personal health data.
assumptions: Communication channel may lack end-to-end encryption or sufficient protection against man-in-the-middle attacks.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; typical for disclosure threats on data flows in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Detectability of health monitoring via traffic analysis
description: Metadata about the communication (timing, volume, endpoints) between Health Analytics Service and Companion Mobile App could allow an observer to detect that health analytics are being performed, inferring sensitive health-related activities.
assumptions: Adversary can monitor network traffic to/from the mobile app.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate based on standard detectability tree for observable data flows.

title: User unawareness of received health insights processing
description: The Companion Mobile App may receive and further process or display the inferred health insights without sufficiently informing or obtaining explicit awareness from the end-user regarding storage, secondary use, or implications of these risk indicators and trend flags.
assumptions: App UI/UX or privacy policy does not clearly communicate the receipt and handling of analytics results.

title: Unawareness of inference implications
description: User (wearer) may not realize the sensitivity or downstream privacy risks of viewing inferred eating-disorder/diabetes indicators on the dashboard, limiting their ability to intervene or consent meaningfully.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate without reference material; based on standard LINDDUN unawareness category for lack of user understanding of data use.

title: Display-induced sensitive disclosure
description: The Companion Mobile App's act of rendering and sharing health-risk trends directly to the user dashboard risks exposing highly personal condition indicators (e.g., eating disorder signals) beyond the intended wearer if screen is visible to bystanders or shared device.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; chosen as plausible disclosure-of-info subnode for visual presentation threats.

title: Unauthorized access or breach at cloud storage
description: The third-party cloud provider receives and stores the full health and location dataset plus analytics models, creating risk of disclosure through insider access, inadequate security, or replication copies.
assumptions: Cloud is untrusted or semi-trusted third party without end-to-end encryption specified.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; typical for disclosure threats on stored data at destination.

title: Regulatory non-compliance for health data hosting
description: Hosting sensitive health and location data at external cloud may violate GDPR, HIPAA or similar without proper data processing agreements, consent or safeguards.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate based on standard LINDDUN Pro non-compliance trees for third-party processing.

title: Lack of transparency on cloud replication
description: The Health Analytics Service shares the complete dataset with the cloud without ensuring data subjects are aware or have consented to third-party hosting and replication.

title: Linkability via traffic to known cloud endpoint
description: Metadata about the data flow (volume, frequency, endpoints) to the cloud provider could link analytics activities to specific health datasets or individuals.
assumptions: Adversary can observe network traffic to the cloud.
uncertainty_note: Node id uncertain; may not be primary for this storage-focused flow.
